## Welcome & logistics

- Syllabus, expectations, grading, project overview (placeholder).
- What this course is: evolution **from populations to ecosystems**, with a genomic and
  plant-centric lens.

## Learning objectives

By the end you should be able to:

- Motivate **why plants** are powerful (and peculiar) systems for evolutionary genomics.
- Sketch the **land-plant phylogeny** and its major clades.
- Name the **key innovations** of the water-to-land transition.
- Define **alternation of generations** and how it shifts across land plants.

# Why plants? {.center}

## Plants are evolutionary extremists

- **Polyploidy & whole-genome duplication** — rampant (preview popgen deck 06 / genome
  architecture).
- **Sessile** — can't flee; adapt in place (local adaptation, popgen deck 05).
- **Diverse mating systems** — selfing, outcrossing, clonality, apomixis (popgen deck 03).
- **Long-lived / huge population sizes / hybridization** — stress-test standard models.
- Economically & ecologically foundational; deep fossil record.

# The green lineage {.center}

## Phylogeny of the Archaeplastida

:::: {.columns}

::: {.column width="50%"}
- Archaeplastida → Viridiplantae (green algae + land plants).
- **Chlorophytes** + **charophytes** (mostly aquatic) → **embryophytes** (land plants,
  ~monophyletic).
- Bullet placeholders: primary endosymbiosis; streptophyte algae as sister to land plants.
:::

# Onto land {.center}

## The water-to-land transition — key innovations

- **Retention of the embryo** (embryophyte = "maternal care"); cuticle; stomata; sporopollenin.
- **Vascular tissue** (xylem/phloem) → tracheophytes; roots, leaves.
- **Seeds** (spermatophytes) → dispersal & desiccation resistance.
- **Flowers** (angiosperms) → pollination & the carpel.

::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE** — timeline/ladder of land-plant key innovations (embryo → vascular → seed →

retention); `Lecture6_gymnosperms.pdf` ~p21 (ovule → seed); `angiosperm-lecture.pdf` ~p19
(flower structure).
:::

## Alternation of generations

- Every land plant alternates a **haploid gametophyte** and a **diploid sporophyte**.
- Evolutionary trend: gametophyte-dominant (bryophytes) → **sporophyte-dominant**
  (vascular plants, seed plants).
- Bullet placeholders: spores vs gametes; heterospory; the reduced gametophyte inside the
  seed/pollen.

# A whistle-stop clade tour {.center}

## The major land-plant clades

- **Bryophytes** (mosses, liverworts, hornworts) — non-vascular, gametophyte-dominant.
- **Lycophytes & ferns** (monilophytes) — seedless vascular plants.
- **Gymnosperms** — conifers, cycads, *Ginkgo*, gnetophytes (~naked seeds).
- **Angiosperms** — flowering plants (~370,000 spp.), incl. the **ANA grade** at the base
  (*Amborella*, Nymphaeales, Austrobaileyales).

::: {.figure-prompt}
**FIGURE** — clade montage / summary tree of land plants. Sources:

(gymnosperm groups), `angiosperm-lecture.pdf` ~p5, `ANAgrade-lecture.pdf` ~p1 (ANA grade).
:::

## Summary

- Plants: polyploid, sessile, mating-system-diverse — evolutionary extremists worth a whole
  course.
- Land-plant evolution = a series of **key innovations** (embryo, vascular tissue, seed,
  flower) on a **green-algal** backbone.
- **Alternation of generations** shifts from gametophyte- to sporophyte-dominance.
